fight: Is ATT&CK version drift an already-solved bookkeeping problem, or a live threat to the validity of CTI analytics?

side_a.position: Solved. MITRE publishes immutable per-release bundles, typed revoked-by edges, retains deprecated objects so dependent workflows do not break, ships diffStix to compute per-release change sets including description diffs, mandates a version stamp in Navigator layers, and funds ATT&CK Sync to flag affected mappings. A consumer who pins a release and applies the crosswalk is fine.
side_a.evidence_type: primary artefacts, read in full from local clones

side_b.position: Not solved. The apparatus is real and, for Enterprise technique identifiers, complete: every revoked identifier carries exactly one successor and none dangle. It is incomplete in four other places. Tactics carry no revocation edges at all, and v19 recycled TA0005 in place — same STIX identifier, renamed from Defense Evasion to Stealth, object version left untouched — while creating TA0112 for the separated concept. Semantic splits are representable only as N:1 merges onto the narrowest survivor, so the crosswalk is lossy by construction rather than incapable. There is no reliable signal for a description rewrite: as a detector of text change the object version field has precision 0.447 and recall 0.641. And the non-destructive guarantee does not extend across domains — Mobile dropped 76 techniques between v2.0 and v3.0 with no tombstone and no successor.

evidence_quality_delta: Both sides rest on the same primary artefacts, and the earlier version of side B overstated its case: the claim that revoked-by cannot express the v19 re-cut is false, since the relation is never one-to-many and the re-cut is encoded as merges. The defensible claim is narrower and still decisive — the crosswalk is lossy, the tactic layer has no crosswalk at all, and adoption is close to zero.
scope_overlap: Genuine disagreement about sufficiency, not about facts. Side A is right that the mechanism exists; side B is right that its coverage is partial and its adoption near-zero.

fight: Is ontology drift material next to the labelling noise that exists at a single pinned version?

side_a.position: Noise dominates. EDR vendors detecting the same behaviour assign disjoint ATT&CK labels within one pinned release, and most ATT&CK groups have no group-specific technique at all, so TTP attribution is weakly identifiable before drift is considered. Drift is a second-order term on a first-order problem.
sources: Saha et al. 2026 (34% of groups have a group-specific technique)

side_b.position: Separable and additive. The controlled experiment holds the labelling process fixed — every condition draws from the same ATT&CK data — so inter-labeller noise is constant across conditions and cancels in the contrasts. Non-identifiability is absorbed by the contemporaneous baseline, which is itself far below 100%. What remains is attributable to vocabulary alone, and it changes the named actor in 72-79% of pre-restructuring observations and in 2.2% even across a single release boundary.

evidence_quality_delta: Side B's evidence is a controlled design that neutralises side A's confounder by construction; side A's evidence is stronger about the absolute difficulty of attribution, which side B concedes.
scope_overlap: Both right, differently scoped: noise bounds absolute accuracy, drift bounds comparability across time. The paper must state that it measures the second and does not claim the first is small.

fight: Does drift land on techniques anyone actually reports, or only on the long tail?

side_a.position: Long tail only. Observed sightings are dominated by a short head of techniques, so churn among rarely used identifiers barely moves any frequency-weighted number.

side_b.position: The head is hit too. Repeating the frozen-capability experiment with techniques weighted by documented prevalence makes the artefact larger, not smaller (17.1-20.0 pp for pre-restructuring portfolios against 12.6-16.5 pp unweighted). The most recent revocation wave took T1562.001, the 33rd most referenced technique in the release it left.

evidence_quality_delta: Side B is direct measurement, but on documentation prevalence rather than telemetry prevalence — the Sightings telemetry is not accessible in this environment, so side A's premise is not tested on its own data.
scope_overlap: Partially scoped apart: documentation prevalence and telemetry prevalence are different quantities. This limitation must be stated rather than argued away.

fight: Was the damage a one-off event in 2020, or is it ongoing?

side_a.position: One-off. Identifier survival since v7.0 is above 0.97 to the present and no post-restructuring cohort has lost half its identifiers. The catastrophic numbers all trace to a single release.
side_a.evidence_type: measurement, primary — and it is our own

side_b.position: Ongoing but bursty. v19.0 revoked 17 live techniques including the entire T1562 family, touching 84 group edges, 155 software edges and 52 of 168 group profiles; v18.0 to v19.0 was 47% bookkeeping for pre-existing groups; 198 techniques changed tactic in one release; and semantic rewriting never stopped — 46.5% of v11.0's ID-stable techniques have edited descriptions by v19.0.

evidence_quality_delta: Even. Both sides are our own measurements over the same corpus, which is exactly why the paper must carry both rather than pick one.
scope_overlap: Genuine tension in interpretation of one dataset. Resolution: identifier churn is episodic; semantic drift is continuous; a risk model must cover both.

fight: Does pinning a release actually restore comparability?

side_a.position: Yes. Pin, declare, and cross-version problems disappear.

side_b.position: Pinning fixes identity, not intension. Descriptions of identifier-stable techniques keep changing with no reliable signal — 494 description edits carried no version bump while 1,072 version bumps carried no text change — so a pinned analytic silently diverges from the meaning its labels now carry. Pinning also freezes the analytic against a vocabulary the field has moved past, which is the trade the paper has to name.

evidence_quality_delta: Side B has the measurement; side A has the operational simplicity.
scope_overlap: Genuine. Pinning is necessary and insufficient.

fight: Are successive CTI benchmarks measuring the same thing?

side_a.position: Yes — same task, same metric, same lab.

side_b.position: No. CTIBench CTI-ATE carries zero sub-technique identifiers and an undeclared v15-era vocabulary; its successor is 70.4% sub-technique labels with a parent-level Jaccard of 0.26 against it. Independently, our own validity analysis finds CTIBench-ATE matches no single ATT&CK release and carries seven Mobile identifiers on rows declared Enterprise.
side_b.evidence_type: primary artefact inspection on both sides

evidence_quality_delta: Side B is artefact-level and was arrived at twice independently, by a corpus audit and by our own validity check.
scope_overlap: No genuine overlap — side A is an assumption nobody defends explicitly once the label files are opened.
